Cc: procurement@bluepeak.com
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: network isolation & evidence for BluePeak RFP

Sergio —

Thanks for taking the RFP. As part of our security review we need a short packet that covers: network isolation topology, how tenant egress is controlled, and a concise threat hypothesis for lateral movement originating in the inference tier. Can you provide diagrams + any short evidence (ACL lists, flow examples) we can include with our evaluation committee?

High level acceptance criteria:
- Diagram showing control plane / data plane boundaries and any ingress/egress choke points
- Statement on sidecar behaviour and KV-cache isolation
- Example of egress allowlist (IPs/domains) or a description of how egress is constrained per-tenant
- 1‑page summary of the most likely attack paths and mitigations

We are on a tight timeline — ideally by EOD Tuesday (20 Jul). If helpful, we can do a quick sync.

Best,
Sara Higgins
Head of Infrastructure Risk
BluePeak Systems

Sergio / Priyom —

Draft items attached and summarized below. Kept everything short for external consumption.

1) Threat hypotheses (rfi-appendix/threat-hypotheses-brief.pdf) — key points:
- Most likely initial foothold: customer-supplied model artifacts or prompt content that triggers resource exhaustion or command injection in model tooling; lateral movement from the inference workload to the host via a misconfigured sidecar is plausible only if sidecar capabilities are escalated.
- High‑impact lateral path: inference worker -> sidecar misconfig -> host network namespace -> control-plane API -> other tenant allocations. Mitigation: strict seccomp profiles for sidecars, immutable image checks, per-tenant network namespaces and host-level egress NATs.

2) KV-cache isolation: sidecars operate with tenant-scoped KV namespaces. Cached keys are tagged with tenant IDs and include a cryptographic salt; runtime enforces read/write tenant checksums. We included the exact wording we publish in customer docs.

3) Egress allowlist (evidence/egress-ip-allowlist.txt) — redacted sample: shows regional NAT ranges, proxy endpoints, and domains blocked/allowed. Enforcement: egress routing is implemented by per-tenant NAT gateway + transparent proxy with ACLs at the VPC layer; we include logging hooks with per-request provenance (request_id, tenant_id, route).

4) Diagram: redwood-diagrams/deployment-overview-v3.png — control plane (VPC peered) is logically separated; data plane worker pools run in tenant-scoped subnets and are not routable to other tenant subnets. Control plane components only talk to worker pools over authenticated mTLS with mutual certs.

Notes for external packet: redact internal host ranges, include CIDR ranges for public-facing egress NATs only. We should also include a short "what we don't expose" bullet list.

I attached the one‑pager and the redacted allowlist. If this looks good I can merge into a single PDF for BluePeak.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sara —

Thanks for the ask. Please find our concise packet attached and a short summary below. We kept the packet redacted to avoid exposing internal host ranges but included the egress CIDR ranges and the evidence you requested.

What we attached:
- deployment-overview-v3.png — diagram showing control-plane/data-plane boundaries and per-tenant subnets
- threat-hypotheses-brief.pdf — one-page summary of likely attack paths and mitigations
- egress-ip-allowlist.txt — redacted example of public NAT ranges and proxy endpoints used for egress

Short answers to your bullets:
- Control/data plane boundaries: Logical separation via VPC segmentation and mTLS-authenticated control channels. Control plane is not routable into tenant private subnets; all control interactions are via authenticated APIs with short-lived certs.
- Sidecar and KV-cache isolation: Sidecars run with minimal capabilities and enforce tenant-scoped KV namespaces. Keys are salted and validated; cross-tenant access is cryptographically rejected by the runtime.
- Egress constraints: Per-tenant NAT gateways + transparent proxies enforce ACLs. We provide redacted CIDR ranges for your allowlist; enforcement is logged per-request and can be surfaced to customers via our Console or by evidence exports.

If you want, we can run the 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow 09:30 PT. Also linking the Drive folder with the packet for your reviewers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Fq_example_shared_folder

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect, Security
Redwood Inference
